questions.prompt: On a position-time (x-t) graph, what does the slope of the curve at a point represent?
options: Distance travelled up to that instant
questions.explanation: The slope of an x-t graph is dx/dt, which by definition is the instantaneous velocity. A steeper slope means faster motion; a horizontal segment means the object is at rest.

questions.prompt: On a velocity-time (v-t) graph, what does the area between the curve and the time axis represent?
questions.explanation: Area under the v-t curve = ∫v·dt = total displacement. If the velocity is constant, the area is a rectangle (v × t); for uniform acceleration it is a trapezium.

questions.prompt: An object's velocity-time graph is a horizontal line at v = 5 m/s. Its acceleration-time (a-t) graph is:
options: A horizontal line at a = 5 m/s²
A straight line with positive slope
questions.explanation: A horizontal v-t line means velocity is constant. Constant velocity means zero acceleration, so the a-t graph is a horizontal line at a = 0 (along the time axis).
